rationale: B wins because it stays closer to the facts while still giving the founder four real reporter shapes. A's riskiest headline, "Allbirds Quietly Dropped 'Eco-Friendly' as Its Main Pitch," asserts a marketing pivot the update does not prove; B's "Allbirds bet its comeback on fewer shoes, not more" is a cleaner contrarian story built from the 40% range cut, store closures, and margin improvement. B still needs proof, but it is less likely to send a founder into a reporter call with a headline that dies at "says who?"
gaps_in_A: "Allbirds Quietly Dropped 'Eco-Friendly' as Its Main Pitch" is an asserted repositioning, not a supplied fact; the set later admits it needs evidence of shifted marketing language.
"brand built on cutting out middlemen" and "D2C IPO cohort" import outside history that is not in the update; source it or cut it.
"The D2C reckoning story has been accumulating for two years" is an unsupported trend peg dressed as context.
The next step says the durability and wholesale angles are "ready to draft once the partner name is confirmed," but durability still needs test data and marketing-copy proof.
gaps_in_B: "durability is the chronic knock against natural-material shoes" is not in the update; either source it or strip it.
"brand that built itself on direct retail" and "DTC-to-wholesale shift" import outside Allbirds positioning; the contrast needs a sourced historical basis.
Several lines imply causality before proof exists: "the first margin improvement followed" and "turnaround plan starts to bite" need the causal breakdown the set asks for.
The materials angle leans on "natural-materials innovation" before third-party validation exists; keep it framed as a company durability claim until the data is real.
